# The steps `tools/ci.ps1` skips FOR WANT OF A CORPUS. Nothing else belongs
# here. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes this file as -ExpectedSkips on every
# runner, and the gate fails on any difference in either direction -- a step
# that skipped for want of a corpus and is not named here, and a step named here
# that did not skip for that reason.
#
# THIS FILE IS NOT A LIST OF THE STEPS ALLOWED TO SKIP. It was until 2026-08-10,
# when the gate ran on windows-latest alone. It stopped being able to be one the
# moment the gate went to three runners, because a flat list cannot say "runs on
# Windows, cannot run on Linux" -- and the two obvious repairs are both worse
# than the disease:
#
#   * one file per platform. Adding 'the built binaries carry their icon and
#     version resource' to the Linux list is a one-line diff that reads as
#     bookkeeping, and nothing anywhere then says the step still runs on
#     Windows. The next amber run makes adding a line the obvious move.
#   * one file with a platform column. Better for review, and it still cannot
#     say WHY: "there is no corpus" and "there is no PE file on Linux" render
#     identically, so a reviewer has no basis on which to push back.
#
# Both add a SECOND, UNVERIFIED claim -- which platforms a step should run on --
# on top of the one thing that is actually verified, which is what the step did.
#
# So the platform half is not written down at all. A step that cannot run off
# Windows declares it in ITS OWN PRECONDITION, as `WindowsOnly { ... }` -- the
# one helper in `tools/ci.ps1` that owns the string 'not windows' -- and the
# gate checks that string against `$IsWindows` rather than believing it: on
# Windows the string is a failure, and off Windows a step that does NOT return
# it must run. NO LINE IN THIS FILE CAN QUIET A PLATFORM SKIP -- that is what the
# split buys, and it is the whole of what it buys.
#
# THE SENTENCE HERE USED TO BE BROADER AND WAS WRONG. It read "there is no line
# anybody can add ANYWHERE to quiet a platform skip", and there is: `WindowsOnly`
# in a portable step's own precondition. Measured on 2026-08-10, by doing it to
# 'gel calibration spline vs SciPy' and pushing -- run 31361991651, whose Linux
# leg reported 5 corpus and EIGHT 'not windows' skips where the honest count is
# seven, and PASSED. Every rule was satisfied: the reason was declared (L1), it
# agreed with the platform (L2), it was not a corpus skip (L3), and the step had
# still run on Windows so the reconciler's X2 was satisfied too. Two platforms of
# coverage gone, nothing red anywhere.
#
# So the boundary, stated as it actually is: these rules catch a step that stops
# running for a reason NOBODY DECLARED -- a wheel that stops building, a
# `pip install` line edited in a hurry, which is the failure that happens. They
# do not catch a human deciding to call a portable step Windows-only. Nothing
# mechanical can, short of the second list this file exists to argue against.
# What holds it is that `WindowsOnly` is one greppable identifier appearing in
# seven places, and `tools/ci.ps1` is reviewed.
#
# See 'THE SKIP DISCIPLINE' at the foot of `tools/ci.ps1` for the three
# per-leg rules, and `tools/reconcile-ledgers.ps1` for the four cross-leg ones,
# which include the only check that can see a step skipping on all three.
#
# WHAT IS LEFT IS THIS FILE, AND IT IS THE SAME ON ALL THREE RUNNERS -- which is
# the test that the split is the right one. "There is no corpus on this machine"
# is a fact about the machine, not about the operating system, so there is
# nothing platform-shaped left in here to need a column.
#
# THIS FILE IS STILL NOT A DESCRIPTION OF A DEVELOPER MACHINE. A workstation
# without SciPy, without WiX, without the wasm target skips more than this and
# that is fine; run the gate with no -ExpectedSkips there. This is the list for a
# runner that has been given everything a runner can be given, and its whole job
# is to make the difference between "the gate passed" and "the gate ran"
# impossible to miss. The gate passed on the author's machine with six steps
# skipped for six releases and no line anywhere said so.
#
# Every name below is here for ONE reason, and it is the same reason: the step
# needs -Corpus, and the corpus is real laboratory .dna and .ab1 files. Those
# are not ours to publish -- Addgene's terms are noncommercial with an
# anti-scraping clause, and a lab's plasmid files belong to that lab -- and
# `.gitignore` bans `*.dna`, `*.ab1`, `*.scf` and `*.ztr` so that a stray
# `git add -A` cannot make them ours either. So this is not a gap to be closed
# by installing something. It is the one honest skip, five times.
#
# THERE IS NO ENTRY FOR A NETWORK SERVICE, and that is deliberate rather than
# lucky. No step in the gate fetches from a third-party data source: `ci.ps1`
# itself names no URL and makes no web call -- its only two `Invoke-WebRequest`
# strings are inside the banned-token lists of the steps that forbid one -- and
# the two feature-database steps it runs are the offline pair, `check_signoff`
# and `check_writer`, over the committed tables. The live-source build moved to
# `.github/workflows/features-live.yml` on 2026-08-07, after EBI timed out twice
# and turned main red for a reason no commit under test had anything to do with,
# and that file's header states the rule: if a step's result would still be true
# tomorrow with the network unplugged, it belongs in ci.yml instead.
#
# So there is no step here to make non-fatal and none to declare skipped for an
# outage. What the `gate` job does need the network for is provisioning --
# cargo's registry, pip, npm, the WiX tool -- and that happens in its own steps,
# before the gate, where a failure is an obvious red install step rather than a
# silent SKIP.
#
# Names are matched exactly, and a name matching no step in the gate is itself a
# failure. So renaming a step below without editing this line goes red, rather
# than quietly reporting that the step has started running.
#
# ONE STEP IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT AND IS WORTH NAMING HERE, because the day it
# starts skipping on Windows the message will be "skipped and its precondition
# declared no reason" and the cause will not be obvious: 'the helper unmangles a
# real 8.3 alias and the arithmetic it replaced does not'. It needs a directory
# reachable through an 8.3 short name, and on a Windows runner it has one for
# free -- `$env:TEMP` is `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp` over a real
# `runneradmin`. That is also what has been exercising the 8.3 half of
# `Get-DirectoryPrefix` incidentally on every run since the gate went green, and
# what caught the defect in run 31325886841 in the first place.
#
# On the Linux and macOS legs that step declares 'not windows' and skips, which
# is checked against the platform and needs no line here. On Windows it must
# RUN, and its precondition deliberately falls back to $false rather than to a
# reason -- so if GitHub ever renames that account to something that fits in
# 8.3, the step skips with no declared reason, the build reds, and the loss of
# coverage gets reported instead of passing silently. That is the whole point of
# the step. Do not reach for a vocabulary entry to make the build green; the
# honest fixes are a runner whose TEMP carries an alias, or a volume with 8.3
# creation enabled so the case can be minted.

wasm module vs native binary
rendered chromatograms agree with their files
chromatograms vs Biopython
digest vs Biopython (real plasmids)
rust reader vs python reader
